title: A string that decodes to a lone surrogate is `bad_message` on a seated connection
notes: CANONICAL.md §2.3 refuses a `\u` escape that resolves to an unpaired surrogate: the value is not representable in UTF-8, which is what a frame's bytes are, so a producer must not write one and a receiver rejects it with `bad_message` rather than let the two readings of the escape become two frames. PROTOCOL.md §5's value rule for a `path` and a `display_name` — non-blank, and free of the Unicode `Cc` category — admits the same value, and §1.1's "a frame conforms when it satisfies both" is what makes the refusal the answer: the frame is one JSON object, so `bad_message` and not `bad_params`. The astral path that follows is the same character written as the pair a producer is allowed to write, and it is accepted and announced, which is what says the refusal is about the unpaired escape and not about a non-ASCII path. Nothing else in the corpus reaches this: an `expect` frame cannot carry one at all, because a vector's own bytes are held to CANONICAL.md §2 and those bytes do not exist, so the rule is only pinnable from the sending side.
